title: Mini-transactions inference wallet — scratchpad
body:
Goal / one-liner:
A lightweight per-session "mini-transaction" wallet that lets apps carve out small, explicit budgets for inference (token or latency credits) and attach soft QoS/behavior rules. Useful for predictable micro-features, in-product trials, and progressive rollouts without changing global quotas or billing rules.

Context / why now:
- Customers ask for predictable, bounded behaviour for micro-interactions (e.g., answer previews, quick Q&A, inline completions) where they want to guarantee cost & latency for each interaction type.
- Current approaches: ad-hoc token limits, global routes, and separate API keys — all heavyweight and error-prone.
- This is a product-first, low-friction primitive that sits between routing policies and billing: developer creates a wallet with credit, attaches it to a session/route, runtime enforces spend and optionally QoS (latency lane, fallback model).

Non-goals:
- Not replacing billing (we still bill usage normally). Wallets are a metering/guardrail primitive, not a separate invoice unit.
- Not an audit ledger for compliance (we log events but not meant for legal accounting).

Core user flows (dev-centric):
1) Create a wallet (console/SDK) specifying token_credits, latency_target_ms, allowed_models (optional), expiry.
2) Attach wallet to session or request via header/sdk param (e.g., x-rdw-wallet: wallet-id).
3) Runtime enforces: when wallet credits exhausted -> trigger fallback policy (fail/soft degrade/route to cheaper model).
4) Dev sees per-wallet telemetry in Console: spent tokens, average latency, fallback counts.
5) Top-up via API or set up auto-topup rule (pay-as-you-go from account balance).

UX sketches (console & API):
- Console: New mini-wallets page under "Hosted API": list wallets, quick create, preview estimate for a prompt (token estimate * model cost).
- Create dialog: name, owner tag, credit amount (tokens or dollars), latency hint (e.g., 100ms), allowed_models (multi-select), expiry, fallback policy.
- SDK: Redwood.createWallet({name, credits: 5000, ttl: 24h, latency_target_ms:200}) -> returns wallet-id.
- Attach: Redwood.request({... , wallet: wallet-id}) or HTTP header x-rdw-wallet.

Rough data model (runtime-friendly):
- Wallet(id, owner, credits_left, credit_unit=[tokens|ms|dollars], latency_target_ms, allowed_models[], fallback_policy, expires_at)
- Lightweight: credits_left stored in a sharded in-memory counter and checkpointed to event log.

Enforcement semantics (early draft):
- Pre-check: runtime checks if wallet has >= estimated_minimum for the request. If not, apply fallback immediately.
- Consumption: at request completion, deduct actual tokens used. For streaming, deduct incrementally on token emission (helps for long responses).
- Latency hint: not a hard SLO but used to pick routing lane; if node cannot meet target, fallback to cheaper/compatible model or signal degrade.
- Race conditions: optimistic pre-check + atomic decrement via single-key increment op on a fast datastore (redis/raft cache). On mismatch, revert & apply fallback.

Product variations / experiments to try:
- Wallet-per-feature: engineering teams mint a wallet for a new feature so they can test traffic without impacting account quotas.
- User-facing credits: surface small trial credits in app (e.g., 10 free completions) store as wallet per user.
- QoS-only wallets: zero tokens but latency_target to influence routing for latency-sensitive requests.
- Metered freebies: auto-topup when wallet below threshold for beta testers.

Value metrics / success signals:
- Developer time to launch micro-feature (target: cut from days to hours).
- Reduction in support incidents tied to unexpected token spend for small features.
- Adoption: percent of teams using wallets for new experiments within 6 weeks of launch.
- Observability UX: perceived usefulness of wallet-level telemetry (qualitative).

Technical considerations & risks:
- Scale: millions of wallets? We should optimize for many ephemeral wallets (TTL + garbage collect). Sharded in-memory counters + TTL eviction.
- Consistency: must avoid double-spend. Use strong atomic ops on hot wallets or approximate budgets (soft enforcement) for tiny wallets. Need to expose semantics clearly.
- Performance: per-request wallet lookup must be cheap; cache wallet policy on serving node with short TTL and background refresh.
- Security: wallet IDs should be unguessable; optional RBAC to limit who can create wallets in org.
- Billing integraton: record wallet->usage mapping for analytics, but billing still aggregates by account key.

Open questions / to decide:
- Primary unit: tokens vs dollars vs micro-transactions (start with tokens).
- Should wallets be transferable between sessions/users? (likely yes, but guarded by ownership).
- Auto-topup UX: immediate topup vs topup-asynchronously. Implications for request flow when credits run out mid-response.
- Fallback strategies: hard fail vs cheaper-model vs truncated response. Need defaults and guidance.
- Retention/visibility: how long do wallet logs live in Console by default?

Next immediate steps (MVP plan):
1) Spike: runtime prototype implementing wallet counter in Redis with atomic decrement, attach-by-header and per-wallet telemetry (2 engineer-weeks).
2) Console mockups + SDK surface for create/attach (1 PM + 1 designer + 1 FE week).
3) Small internal beta: 2 product teams run experiments for 4 weeks.
4) Measure, iterate on pre-check semantics and fallback UX.

Notes / references / rough tickets:
- Experiment idea came from slack thread #prod-econ 2025-11-10 (Evan).
- See JIRA-MLINF-842 for initial acceptance criteria draft.
- PoC repo branch: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proto branch "wallet-poC" PR #297.

Quick TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Sketch Console create dialog (low-fidelity).
- [ ] Talk to billing (Evan) about mapping wallets->analytics export.
- [ ] Validate atomic counter approach with infra (Kai).
- [ ] Draft user stories for beta teams.

Random thoughts (brain dump):
- Could be a neat primitive for "pay-per-suggestion" UI where each suggestion consumes a tiny credit.
- Combine with evaluation harness to auto-revoke wallets that cause quality regressions (cool but later).
- Be explicit in docs: wallets do NOT change invoice granularity; they are controls, not new billing product.

End.
